chapter: Failure in St. Louis and the Omaha bands
title: Lloyd Hunter's band led by Anna Mae Winburn, with Red Rivers
summary: Thompson recalls Anna Mae Winburn directing Lloyd Hunter's band with singer Red Rivers, her later Sweethearts of Rhythm connection, and the entertainer routine.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving

blocks.x: Well, how long did you stay with Nat Towles. And I see you went to Floyd Roy's band from Nat Towles. How did that happen?
Here again I'm lost for statistics. I don't know time, I just can't -- you see --
To think back that far you can't remember how long.
I'm not good at statistics. I would have to really go back and get records and so forth, which I don't have personally.

But I'd also like to mention while we're talking about that, that this first band that I played in had a very, very important figure in the world of entertainment in the midwest, in the person of Anna Mae Windburn.
She was a girl singer who directed Lloyd Hunter's band.

Yes. She was very good at this too. She handled the baton to the beat of jazz music, and she sang. Very, very pretty girl, very attractive girl. And she led the band while we played, she was part of the attraction.
Did they ever made any records?
She later on went on to lead the girls' band. You know, they had several --
That's right. That was Anna Mae Windburn, and she was the girl vocalist in the band that I first played with. Lloyd Hunter was the first good professional band that I played with.

And she was the singer and band leader in that group. We also had another singer by the name of Red Rivers who did a lot of tunes of entertainment, like one of his famous songs was Old Man Moses Kicked the Bucket.
Old Man Moses. Old Man Moses. Old Man Moses, Old Man Moses (Singing).
I remember that That Stuff made a hit with it too.
Well, this fella was very proficient at doing these entertainment type of numbers, and the two of them led the band.
